title: A negative externality: overproduction
caption: The market produces where demand meets private cost, at 40 units. When each unit also imposes £20 of cost on third parties, the social cost curve lies above it and the best level is 30. The 10 extra units are overproduction.
alt: Demand and two upward curves, private cost and social cost £20 higher. Demand meets private cost at 40 units and £60; it meets social cost at 30 units and £70. The gap between 30 and 40 is shaded as overproduction.
description: Private cost slopes up; the market price and quantity are where it meets demand: 40 units at £60.
Social cost is private cost plus £20 of external cost.
Social benefit equals social cost at 30 units, so the market overproduces by 10 units.
